reasoning_traces.think:
SHAPEffects operates by iteratively removing features whose local SHAP contributions correlate with prediction errors in the validation set, thereby identifying variables whose influence has become counterproductive under concept shift. It leverages the duality between global feature importance and local prediction fidelity. In static regimes, this method matches standard selectors because SHAP values remain stable. However, under concept shift, SHAP values reflect outdated relationships, causing misalignment with actual prediction errors. The core insight is that a variable’s global importance does not guarantee its continued utility; local error analysis reveals when a variable's learned effect now pushes predictions in the wrong direction. This failure mode—where globally important features become locally harmful—is common in time-series forecasting and regime-switching environments. SHAPEffects mitigates this by focusing on the validation set, where future performance is evaluated. The method uses a two-phase backward selection process: first, filtering out noise-like variables through permutation; second, iteratively dropping variables whose aggregate effect on validation errors is negative. This approach ensures that only features contributing positively to current predictions are retained. The empirical success of SHAPEffects in both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates its robustness to sudden and incremental shifts.

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring that variables with overlapping SHAP profiles do not coexist in the same iteration. Leakage is prevented by restricting SHAP computation to the validation set, avoiding data leakage from test or training sets. Veto conditions arise when a variable's effect is indeterminate (zero SHAP) or when its influence is consistently negative across all validation points, indicating pure noise.
